title: X replies to Jacob Coxon's Anthropic resignation thread
artefact_title: Jacob Coxon's seven-tweet resignation thread on X
central_claim: Neither OpenAI nor Anthropic is acting responsibly with frontier AI, and both are racing towards dangerous self-improving superintelligence.
capture_method: X gives no API or export route, so every reply was retrieved through a signed-in browser session reading the on-page feed directly, across all four sort views the platform offers. Each view independently stops rendering new items after a few hundred, regardless of how many replies the post has, so the 25,219 replies across all seven posts were never fully reachable: 2,639 items were retrieved and 2,480 remained after excluding promoted content and Coxon's own thread posts. Coverage per post ranged from 2.6% (the root post, with 20,553 replies) to 93% (the smallest follow-up post, with 250 replies). Because coverage is such a sparse, sort-view-selected slice of each post's replies, a reply's parent_id almost never resolves to another row in this same file (0 of 1,946 non-blank parent_id values do); threading is therefore not preserved at all, and comments.csv leaves parent_id and depth blank on every row, the same convention used for METR and Soares.

spot_check.note: Random 40-reply sample checked against the codebook on stance, frame, format reaction and emotion before publication; 38/40 agreed. Which specific rows were sampled was not recorded at row level, so comments.csv's spot_checked column is false throughout; this field is the only record of the check.

coders: Claude (claude-sonnet-5), parallel batches of about 190 (2,391 replies carrying text)

changelog.note: Initial import: 2,480 rows from the coded TSV export, transformed into contract shape (columns renamed to the mentions_<thing> convention, coder/spot_checked/correction_note columns added, parent_id/depth blanked since they do not resolve within this sample, reply_count and reposts kept as study-specific extra columns after correction_note, matching Cotra's reply_count precedent).

licence: CC BY 4.0 (coding and compilation; comment text remains its authors')
notes: The first study in this series not about the OpenAI/Hugging Face agent-swarm incident: Coxon's thread is about his own resignation, a different artefact entirely, so this study's series is 'resignation reception' rather than 'agent-swarm reception'. format_reaction here (mock/condescended/imitates/praise/none) matches the broader vocabulary shared by Cotra, METR and Soares, not the narrower interview-specific one (none/praise/criticism) that only the Amanpour segment uses; marked shared:true in codebook.json accordingly. 89 rows have no text (GIF/image/sticker-only replies the platform exposed no text for) and are marked coder=not_coded_empty_stub with placeholder codes (stance na, frame format_only, format_reaction none, emotion neutral), per the contract's stub exemption; they still carry real likes/reposts/reply_count/timestamp data, unlike some stub rows in other studies.
